features.description: Turn-lock (backend, correctness first) — best-effort CAS on the existing group_sessions doc; acquire before the ADK run, release in finally, 409 on collision, 90s TTL steal. The guard that prevents the concurrent-turn race (bug #3). MUST land first.
acceptance_criteria: acquire_turn_lock best-effort CAS: while one token holds a non-stale lock, another token is refused (returns False)
A locked send surfaces HTTP 409 (turn_in_progress) from the student stream route before the SSE body starts; after release the next send succeeds
release_turn_lock clears only when the holding token matches; a foreign token cannot unlock a live turn
A lock older than the 90s TTL is stealable (a crashed/closed-tab turn does not wedge the group)
A proactive turn is skipped (skipped=True) while a student turn holds the lock; teacher/individual callers bypass the lock entirely
cd backend && make lint && make test-fast green
features.notes: DONE. Lock rides group_sessions doc (acquire/release/get_turn_lock + TURN_LOCK_TTL_SECONDS=90). process_skill_request became a thin locking wrapper over renamed _run_skill_turn — gated on user.group_id so teachers bypass. TurnLockedError -> 409 in student route (fast_api_app.py), -> skipped=True in proactive greet. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: firestore abstraction exposes NO transactions by design (in-memory client: 'v6 doesn't use them'), so the lock is a best-effort read-check-write + TTL, same posture as sibling set_active_session_for_group. Design/plan wording 'transactional CAS' softened to 'best-effort CAS' — needs a docs touch-up at sprint end. 2431 backend tests pass; lint clean.

features.description: Live chat sync (fullstack, the headline) — GET /api/auth/group/pulse {revision,turnInFlight,turnStartedAt} + useGroupPulse poll (~2.5s active, back off hidden) + refetch useSessionMessages on revision change (watcher-gated) + composer lock/queue on turnInFlight. Fixes bug #1 (no live sync); bug #2 (ghost context) falls out.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/auth/group/pulse returns {revision,turnInFlight,turnStartedAt}, group-auth'd (keyed off caller group_id), zero LLM; revision bumps after a turn commits; turnInFlight reflects the non-stale M0 lock; scoped to caller group; 404 for non-group
Device B (pure watcher, same group+activity, not reloaded) sees device A's new user turn AND the tutor reply within one poll (~2.5s of commit)
While a groupmate's turn is in flight, this device's composer shows 'A classmate is asking the tutor…'; a message typed meanwhile is queued and auto-sent when the turn clears

useSessionMessages refetches silently (no loading flash) only on a FORWARD revision jump, and only for a pure watcher (messages.length===0) so ChatMessageList's un-deduped live block can't double; sentinel filter preserved
cd backend && make lint && make test-fast green AND cd frontend && npm run quality:check green
features.notes: DONE, with two reality-adjustments from the plan: (1) pulse endpoint is GET /api/auth/group/pulse?activityId= (keyed off caller group_id like raise-hand) NOT /sessions/{id}/pulse — avoids needing a session_id->group+activity mapping; declared before GET /{group_id} so it isn't shadowed. (2) revision source: chat_sessions.turnCount is flushed only every N turns (session.py:359), so it can't be the signal; instead a turn_revision counter on the group_sessions doc bumped at turn completion (in the M0 finally, before release) — race-free because the lock serializes turns. KNOWN BOUNDARY: live message refetch is watcher-only (a device that has itself sent relies on its live stream; ChatMessageList renders restored history + live as two un-deduped blocks so a sender-side refetch would duplicate). The turn-lock (turn-based) covers the interaction case. Full bidirectional live-refetch (dedupe the merge) is a documented follow-up. No live token-mirroring (design's stated v1 boundary). Backend 85 pass; frontend quality:check exit 0 (lint+tsc+vitest 22 hook tests+build).

features.description: Workbench state sync (fullstack) — add workbenchRevision to the pulse (bump on iframe-context write); other devices refetch iframe-context and reconcile element state (last-write-wins with convergence). Fixes bug #4 (workbench clobber). Groupmate trust-cards surface in the shared thread.
acceptance_criteria: The pulse carries workbenchRevision which bumps on each iframe-context write
Device A edits the table/calculator -> device B's workbench reflects it within a poll
Device B's subsequent edit does not silently erase A's; both devices converge to the same state (last-write-wins documented)
A groupmate's 'shared with the AI' trust-card is visible in the shared thread
cd backend && make lint && make test-fast green AND cd frontend && npm run quality:check green
features.notes: DEFERRED by decision (M, 2026-07-01) — needs its own scoping. Turned out bigger than the ~1-1.5d estimate: live workbench sync requires every workbench element (table/calculator/checklist/...) to accept EXTERNAL state updates (they currently own their local state), plus a real collaborative-edit product call (two kids editing one table = conflicts). The pulse already reserves a workbenchRevision slot; the hard part is the element-side controlled-state refactor, not the plumbing.
